RagShortTexts: The Burgundian-Castilian house quarterly paired castles and lions under Alfonso X's legal.

Variants.Content: Quartering castles and lions to herald the union of Castile and León, the House of Burgundy-Ivrea ruled under Alfonso X 'the Wise'. Alfonso promulgated Las Siete Partidas, a landmark synthesis of Roman law affirming monarchical sovereignty, while exhausting royal silver to secure election as Holy Roman Emperor.
Great magnates (ricoshombres) resented fiscal exactions and centralized jurisprudence, sparking recurring feudal coalitions that threatened crown authority across Toledo and Burgos.
Alfonso patronized poets and astronomers, orchestrating the Alfonsine Tables and Cantigas de Santa Maria, creating a glorious vernacular renaissance in Castile.
